name: ESA
description: European Space Agency. Highly scientific EO roles requiring PhD and publications. Direct target for climate applications scientist profiles.
relevance: Direct match for Earth observation scientists. ESA's Climate Office and Phi-Lab run cutting-edge research in climate data products using Sentinel, MODIS, and multispectral imagery — exactly the technical stack you know.

name: EUMETSAT
description: Operational satellite agency focused on meteorological EO products. Stable institutional roles.
relevance: Strong fit for remote sensing backgrounds with meteorological data experience. Works with Meteosat and Sentinel-3 products for operational climate monitoring.

name: ECMWF
description: Numerical weather prediction centre. Very research-oriented. Atmospheric and ocean science roles.
relevance: ERA5 reanalysis and climate projections team. If you work with ERA5 or CMIP6 data, ECMWF is a natural environment. Roles exist in data science applied to NWP output.

name: Copernicus / CLMS
description: EU Earth observation programme operated via ESA and EUMETSAT. Produces land, marine, atmosphere and climate change monitoring services.
relevance: Land surface and climate monitoring products built on Sentinel data — direct overlap with remote sensing workflows. Contracting opportunities via service providers.

name: ECB
description: Frankfurt. Climate Scientist role in the Climate Change Centre. Macro-financial climate risk. Less technical than EO roles.
relevance: Relevant if interested in macro-level climate risk and policy. Roles are more economics-facing than technical, but the team does work with physical risk metrics.

name: Deltares
description: Netherlands. Research institute specializing in water, subsurface and infrastructure. Flood and coastal modelling, hydrodynamics, SWAN model.
relevance: Flood modelling with Python and open-source geospatial tools. Strong culture of applied research. Overlap with coastal remote sensing and hydrological datasets.

name: Kayrros
description: EO analytics company using MODIS, VIIRS, Sentinel, SAR for climate risk and emissions monitoring. Science-first culture.
relevance: Exact overlap: MODIS, VIIRS, SAR, Sentinel are their core stack. Strong Python culture, close to research. One of the best fits for a climate data scientist with remote sensing depth.

name: Hydrosat
description: Thermal infrared satellite constellation for agriculture and drought monitoring. US-based, strong engineering culture.
relevance: Niche thermal infrared EO work. Relevant for drought and water stress monitoring. US-based, which is a consideration if seeking European roles.

name: Planet
description: Commercial satellite operator. Very EO-focused. Strong engineering and data science culture.
relevance: Strong Python and computer vision culture. Less climate-specific than others, more focused on high-cadence optical imagery. Relevant if open to broad EO data science.

name: Lobelia Earth
description: Barcelona-based. Physical climate risk projections via EO. Strong science team, works with insurers like MAPFRE.
relevance: Barcelona location, EO + physical risk intersection, works directly with insurers. Very strong fit for a climate data scientist interested in parametric products.

name: Tesselo
description: Lisbon. Satellite imagery and AI for wildfire and forest risk. Working on parametric insurance applications.
relevance: Combines SAR/EO with parametric insurance triggers. Python-heavy team. Wildfire focus is a growing segment in parametric. Lisbon-based.

name: ICEYE
description: Finland. World's largest SAR satellite constellation. Flood, wildfire and hurricane monitoring for insurers and governments. Very strong EO + insurance intersection.
relevance: SAR specialist with direct insurance applications. ICEYE products are used by insurers for parametric flood and wildfire triggers — strong overlap with remote sensing + insurance interest.

name: Ocean Ledger
description: Coastal EO analytics for shoreline change and coastal risk. Early stage (pre-seed). Niche but relevant.
relevance: Coastal remote sensing niche. Early stage means risk but also influence. Relevant if interested in blue-carbon and sea-level risk.

name: Mitiga Solutions
description: Barcelona. Physics-based climate risk models using CMIP6 and HPC. Spun out of Barcelona Supercomputing Center. Science-first culture.
relevance: Spun out of BSC — same culture as academic climate science, but applied to insurance and finance. CMIP6 workflows, HPC, Python. Barcelona location is a bonus.

name: Climate X
description: London. Physical risk and loss modelling using EO and geospatial stack. Multiple open roles now. Series A from Google Ventures.
relevance: Actively hiring data scientists. Uses EO + geospatial stack to quantify physical climate risk for financial institutions. GV backing means growth trajectory.

name: Moody's RMS
description: London. Catastrophe modelling with a team of 50+ PhD scientists. Climate hazards team works on tropical cyclones, floods, storm surge.
relevance: Established cat modelling firm with a large science team. Climate hazard work on floods and tropical cyclones overlaps with hydrology and remote sensing backgrounds.

name: Verisk / AIR
description: London and Boston. Cat model development and consulting. More insurance-oriented than scientific.
relevance: Large established player. Science roles exist but the culture is more actuarial/consulting. Good for exposure to insurance, less ideal for deep science.

name: Fathom
description: Bristol. World authority on flood hazard modelling. CMIP6-based climate-conditioned flood models. Partnered with Swiss Re and Climate X.
relevance: Flood modelling authority. CMIP6 climate-conditioned models and hydrological expertise are directly relevant. Partnered with insurers so there is applied science output.

name: JBA Risk Management
description: UK. Flood science specialist. Global flood models with CMIP6 climate projections. Works with reinsurers, insurers and World Bank on parametric sovereign risk.
relevance: Flood modelling + parametric sovereign risk — a rare combination. CMIP6 projections in a real insurance context. Strong science culture for a UK firm.

name: Reask
description: Physics-based tropical cyclone modelling and catastrophe analytics for insurers and reinsurers. Science-driven, parametric-ready.
relevance: Small, science-first team building physics-based cyclone models. Direct application to parametric reinsurance. Strong fit if interested in tropical hazards.

name: Jupiter Intelligence
description: USA. Climate risk analytics using science-based models. Works with governments and corporations.
relevance: Science-based climate risk analytics. Python-heavy. US-based but remote roles sometimes available. More consulting-facing than pure research.

name: Descartes Underwriting
description: Paris. Parametric insurance using physics-based models and satellite data. 150 people, 60+ countries.
relevance: EO data + parametric triggers at scale. Paris-based. Uses satellite data to build parametric products — strong fit for a remote sensing scientist transitioning to insurance.

name: Floodbase
description: NYC. Parametric flood insurance using satellite flood detection. MODIS and VIIRS stack. Direct overlap with your remote sensing background.
relevance: Exact overlap: uses MODIS, VIIRS and SAR for parametric flood triggers — the same data stack as your background. One of the strongest technical fits in the landscape.

name: Arbol
description: NYC. Parametric climate risk platform and insurance. Uses dClimate data infrastructure. Covers drought, hurricane, frost and more.
relevance: Broad parametric coverage across multiple perils. Uses climate data platforms. US-based but the data product side may have remote roles.

name: Kettle
description: Bermuda. Parametric reinsurance for wildfires and hurricanes. ML-based underwriting.
relevance: ML-based parametric reinsurance. More modelling / actuarial culture than EO science. Relevant if interested in the reinsurance side of parametric products.

name: Repath Earth
description: Hamburg. Physical climate risk analytics for infrastructure portfolios — power grids, solar, wind, data centers. Spun out of CEN (University of Hamburg). Clients include Enel and E.ON.
relevance: ML hazard models + EO data translated into financial impacts (CapEx, OpEx, AAL) at asset level. Science-born, infrastructure-facing. Relevant if interested in climate risk for energy transition assets.

name: AON
description: London. Cat risk consulting and parametric insurance. Large team. More actuarial than scientific.
relevance: Large consulting shop. Science roles exist in the cat modelling practice but the culture is finance-facing. Better as a later career move after building insurance credibility.

name: Swiss Re
description: Zurich. Global reinsurer with parametric products and a growing climate risk science team. More actuarial than scientific for most roles.
relevance: Climate risk science team exists but most science roles are finance/actuarial facing. Better fit after gaining insurance experience.

name: Resallience
description: Montpellier. Physical climate risk assessment for real assets and insurance. French market, small team.
relevance: Small team working on physical risk for real estate and insurance. French market focus. Relevant if based in France or open to Montpellier.

name: The Climate Data Factory
description: Paris. Climate downscaling and projections based on CMIP6. Scientific and applied.
relevance: CMIP6 downscaling is a core skill overlap. Paris-based, scientific culture. Produces climate projection data products used across sectors.

name: First Street
description: NYC. Physical climate risk data for real estate and finance. Strong data science culture.
relevance: Flood and fire risk data products for financial institutions. Python-heavy data science team. US-based but well known in the climate risk data space.

name: Cervest
description: London. Climate intelligence platform. Downscaling and risk scoring. Has gone through restructuring.
relevance: Climate risk scoring platform. Some EO integration. Has gone through restructuring so check current team size before applying.

name: Sust Global
description: Geospatial AI platform for physical climate risk analytics. EO-based. Works with financial institutions and asset managers.
relevance: EO + geospatial AI for physical risk. Relevant tech stack. US-based. Works with asset managers who need climate risk data products.

name: Betterview
description: Munich. Geospatial property intelligence for insurers using aerial and satellite imagery. More property inspection than climate science.
relevance: EO applied to property insurance — less climate science, more inspection and underwriting support. Lower fit unless interested in property risk specifically.

name: dClimate
description: Decentralized climate data marketplace. Open data infrastructure for parametric insurance and climate analytics.
relevance: Open climate data infrastructure. More data engineering and platform than science. Relevant if interested in climate data access and parametric product development.
